notes.subject: car
notes.text: Unique car with two metal bars marked by thick black stripes and a white hood visible at the front.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Most poles are square concrete with a reverse L at the top; round or octagonal ones are rarer.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Pale yellow on top and white below, a bit like New Jersey plates; front plates are not required.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Stop signs say PARE, the South American form, and many signs sit on yellow posts.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Smooth asphalt that is noticeably darker than in neighbouring countries.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Only the capital and the northern city of Santiago are covered.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Mountains to the north mean you are in Santiago de los Caballeros.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Yellow traffic light poles are typical of Santiago.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: The capital has tall buildings and wide avenues, more developed than elsewhere.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Street name signs in the capital often carry the letters ADN, for the National District.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Black-and-purple pole markings appear only around the capital.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Outskirts show narrow dirt tracks, whitish dirt, dried green shrubs and roadside debris.
